mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 6.0% signals a tightening labor market, which typically precedes stronger corporate earnings and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to improved corporate outlook.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 40% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST rise.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% annually, it triggers concerns about central bank tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as investors price in higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in less than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 indicates a contraction in manufacturing and services, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants react to deteriorating economic conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in less than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust labor market, which typically precedes higher consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 40% of instances when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) exceed their 12-month moving average, it signals sustained consumer spending strength, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to improve.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in less than 40% of instances when RSAFS > 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% signals an imminent monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%.
